### Configure bun-create setup lifecycle scripts in package.json

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/templating/create.mdx

Defines custom setup hooks such as `preinstall`, `postinstall`, and `start` in the `bun-create` field of a local template's `package.json`.

```json
{
  "name": "@bun-examples/simplereact",
  "version": "0.0.1",
  "main": "index.js",
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^17.0.2",
    "react-dom": "^17.0.2"
  },
  "bun-create": {
    "preinstall": "echo 'Installing...'", // a single command
    "postinstall": ["echo 'Done!'"], // an array of commands
    "start": "bun run echo 'Hello world!'"
  }
}
```

### Install project dependencies with bun install

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/solidstart.mdx

Navigate into the project directory and install the required dependencies.

```sh
cd my-app
bun install
```

--------------------------------

### start(options?)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/streams.mdx

Configures and starts the sink buffer with options such as preallocated size and streaming behavior.

```APIDOC
## start(options?)

### Description
Starts or restarts the sink with optional configuration for buffer sizing and output formats.

### Signature
```ts
start(options?: {
  asUint8Array?: boolean;
  highWaterMark?: number;
  stream?: boolean;
}): void;
```

### Parameters
- **options** (object) - Optional configuration object.
  - **asUint8Array** (boolean) - Optional. If `true`, returns a `Uint8Array` when streaming or ending.
  - **highWaterMark** (number) - Optional. Preallocates an internal buffer of this size to improve performance when chunk sizes are small.
  - **stream** (boolean) - Optional. On `flush()`, returns the written data as a `Uint8Array` or `ArrayBuffer`, and restarts writes from the beginning of the buffer.
```

### Install Bun and dependencies in GitHub Actions workflow

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/install/cicd.mdx

```yaml
name: my-workflow
jobs:
  my-job:
    name: my-job
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # ...
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 # [!code ++]

      # run any `bun` or `bunx` command
      - run: bun install # [!code ++]
```

```

--------------------------------

### Install Bun

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/README.md

Install Bun using the recommended shell script, PowerShell on Windows, npm, Homebrew, or Docker.

```sh
# with install script (recommended)
curl -fsSL https://bun.com/install | bash

# on windows
powershell -c "irm bun.sh/install.ps1 | iex"

# with npm
npm install -g bun

# with Homebrew
brew tap oven-sh/bun
brew install bun

# with Docker
docker pull oven/bun
docker run --rm --init --ulimit memlock=-1:-1 oven/bun
```

### Filter workspace installations with --filter

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx

Target or exclude specific workspace packages when running bun install in a monorepo setup.

```bash
# Install dependencies for all workspaces except `pkg-c`
bun install --filter '!pkg-c'

# Install dependencies for only `pkg-a` in `./packages/pkg-a`
bun install --filter './packages/pkg-a'
```

### Create an Express server in server.ts

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/express.mdx

Define a root GET route and start an Express HTTP server listening on port 8080.

```ts
import express from "express";

const app = express();
const port = 8080;

app.get("/", (req, res) => {
  res.send("Hello World!");
});

app.listen(port, () => {
  console.log(`Listening on port ${port}...`);
});
```

# View package dependencies

# View package homepage

```

### Get elapsed process time with Bun.nanoseconds()

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/utils.mdx

Returns the number of nanoseconds elapsed since the current Bun process started. Useful for high-precision timing and benchmarking.

```ts
Bun.nanoseconds();
// => 7288958
```

--------------------------------

### Basic HTTP Server Setup with Bun.serve

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/http/server.mdx

Demonstrates defining static, dynamic, and method-specific routes using the routes configuration object, which requires Bun v1.2.3+. Includes a fallback fetch handler for unmatched routes.

```ts
const server = Bun.serve({
  // `routes` requires Bun v1.2.3+
  routes: {
    // Static routes
    "/api/status": new Response("OK"),

    // Dynamic routes
    "/users/:id": req => {
      return new Response(`Hello User ${req.params.id}!`);
    },

    // Per-HTTP method handlers
    "/api/posts": {
      GET: () => new Response("List posts"),
      POST: async req => {
        const body = await req.json();
        return Response.json({ created: true, ...body });
      },
    },

    // Wildcard route for all routes that start with "/api/" and aren't otherwise matched
    "/api/*": Response.json({ message: "Not found" }, { status: 404 }),

    // Redirect from /blog/hello to /blog/hello/world
    "/blog/hello": Response.redirect("/blog/hello/world"),

    // Serve a file by lazily loading it into memory
    "/favicon.ico": Bun.file("./favicon.ico"),
  },

  // (optional) fallback for unmatched routes:
  // Required if Bun's version < 1.2.3
  fetch(req) {
    return new Response("Not Found", { status: 404 });
  },
});

console.log(`Server running at ${server.url}`);
```

### Omitting marker in indented code block within block quote

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/js/bun/md/spec.txt

Omitting '>' in front of lines intended for an indented code block ends the block quote and starts a separate code block.

```example
>     foo
    bar
.
<blockquote>
<pre><code>foo
</code></pre>
</blockquote>
<pre><code>bar
</code></pre>
```

--------------------------------

### Install benchmark dependencies and run benchmark suites

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/bench/README.md

Run from the bench directory to install benchmark dependencies like mitata, then execute various benchmark suites. Set environment variables like BUN or edit .env to benchmark custom binary versions.

```bash
# run from this directory. bench/ has its own package.json and bun.lock,
# the repo root does not install benchmark dependencies such as mitata.
bun install

bun run ffi
bun run log
bun run gzip
bun run async
bun run sqlite

# to use custom version of bun/deno/node binary
BUN=path/to/bun bun run ffi
# or edit .env file
```

### Download and install LLVM for ARM64

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/project/building-windows.mdx

Downloads the ARM64 Windows installer for LLVM 21.1.8 from GitHub releases and performs a silent installation.

```powershell
# Download and install LLVM for ARM64
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/releases/download/llvmorg-21.1.8/LLVM-21.1.8-woa64.exe" -OutFile "$env:TEMP\LLVM-21.1.8-woa64.exe"
Start-Process -FilePath "$env:TEMP\LLVM-21.1.8-woa64.exe" -ArgumentList "/S" -Wait
```

--------------------------------

### Install LLVM 21 on Ubuntu/Debian

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

Runs the automatic LLVM installation script to install LLVM 21 on Ubuntu or Debian distributions.

```bash
$ # LLVM has an automatic installation script that is compatible with all versions of Ubuntu
$ wget https://apt.llvm.org/llvm.sh -O - | sudo bash -s -- 21 all
```

### Configure global installation paths in bunfig.toml

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/add.mdx

Sets custom installation and binary link directories for packages installed globally via Bun.

```toml
[install]
# where `bun add --global` installs packages
globalDir = "~/.bun/install/global"

# where globally-installed package bins are linked
globalBinDir = "~/.bun/bin"
```

```toml
[serve.static]

```sh
$ bun index.html

--------------------------------

### Filter package installation with bun install

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/filter.mdx

Use `--filter` with positive and negative glob or path patterns to selectively install dependencies for monorepo workspaces.

```bash
# Install dependencies for all workspaces except `pkg-c`
bun install --filter '!pkg-c'

# Install dependencies for packages in `./packages` (`pkg-a`, `pkg-b`, `pkg-c`)
bun install --filter './packages/*'

# Save as above, but exclude the root package.json
bun install --filter '!./' --filter './packages/*'
```

### Scaffold a new project with bun init

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/templating/init.mdx

Scaffold a new project interactively by providing a directory name. Press enter to accept the default options or provide the `-y` flag to auto-accept defaults without prompting.

### Install @sentry/bun SDK

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/sentry.mdx

Install the official Sentry SDK package for Bun.

```sh
bun add @sentry/bun
```

--------------------------------

### Specify installation linker strategy via CLI

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/isolated-installs.mdx

Pass `--linker isolated` or `--linker hoisted` to `bun install` to choose between strict dependency isolation and traditional hoisted installation.

```bash
# Use isolated installs
bun install --linker isolated

# Use traditional hoisted installs
bun install --linker hoisted
```

--------------------------------

### Start development server with bun --bun run dev

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/sveltekit.mdx

Navigate to the project directory and start the Vite dev server using Bun runtime. Omit the `--bun` flag to run with Node.js instead.

```sh
cd my-app
bun --bun run dev
```

```txt

  Forced re-optimization of dependencies

    ➜  Local:   http://localhost:5173/
    ➜  Network: use --host to expose
    ➜  press h + enter to show help
```

### Initialize project and install Drizzle

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/drizzle.mdx

Initialize a fresh Bun project and install `drizzle-orm` alongside `drizzle-kit` as a development dependency.

```sh
bun init -y
bun add drizzle-orm
bun add -D drizzle-kit
```

--------------------------------

### Install and import an npm package using an alias

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/install/npm-alias.mdx

Install an npm package under an alias with `bun add <alias>@npm:<package>`. After installation, import the package using the alias name in your code.

```sh
bun add my-custom-name@npm:zod
```

```ts
import { z } from "my-custom-name";

z.string();
```

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/packages/bun-inspector-protocol/README.md

Installs the bun-inspector-protocol package using Bun or alternative package managers.

```bash
bun add bun-inspector-protocol
# npm install bun-inspector-protocol
# yarn add bun-inspector-protocol
# pnpm add bun-inspector-protocol
```

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/packages/bun-plugin-svelte/README.md

Install bun-plugin-svelte as a development dependency using the Bun package manager.

```sh
$ bun add -D bun-plugin-svelte

```

### Install Bun with Scoop

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/installation.mdx

Installs Bun on Windows using the Scoop package manager.

```bash
scoop install bun
```

--------------------------------

### Build and Run Production Server

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/bundler/fullstack.mdx

Builds the fullstack application for production targeting Bun and starts the server with NODE_ENV set to production.

```bash
# Build for production
bun build --target=bun --production --outdir=dist ./server/index.ts

# Run production server
NODE_ENV=production bun dist/index.js
```

--------------------------------

### Add build and start scripts for Nitro in package.json

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/tanstack-start.mdx

Define build and start scripts in package.json to run Nitro's generated output using Bun. The start script is not required when deploying to Vercel.

```json
  {
    "scripts": {
      "build": "bun --bun vite build", // [!code ++]
      // The .output files are created by Nitro when you run `bun run build`.
      // Not necessary when deploying to Vercel.
      "start": "bun run .output/server/index.mjs" // [!code ++]
    }
  }
```

--------------------------------

### Common bunx execution examples

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/snippets/cli/bunx.mdx

Demonstrates common tasks with bunx, including running migrations, targeting specific package versions, specifying different binary names with -p, and forcing Bun execution with --bun.

```bash
# Run Prisma migrations
bunx prisma migrate

# Format a file with Prettier
bunx prettier foo.js

# Run a specific version of a package
bunx uglify-js@3.14.0 app.js

# Use --package when binary name differs from package name
bunx -p @angular/cli ng new my-app

# Force running with Bun instead of Node.js, even if the executable contains a Node shebang
bunx --bun vite dev foo.js
```

--------------------------------

### Install Bun on macOS and Linux with curl

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/installation.mdx

Installs Bun via the official shell script. Linux environments require the unzip package (`sudo apt install unzip`) and recommend kernel 5.6 or higher.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://bun.com/install | bash
```

--------------------------------

### Serve static in-memory file vs filesystem file routes

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/http/routing.mdx

Use `await Bun.file(path).bytes()` to buffer content in RAM at startup for zero filesystem I/O with ETag support, or pass `Bun.file(path)` directly for streaming reads and built-in 404 handling.

```typescript
Bun.serve({
  routes: {
    // Static route - content is buffered in memory at startup
    "/logo.png": new Response(await Bun.file("./logo.png").bytes()),

    // File route - content is read from filesystem on each request
    "/download.zip": new Response(Bun.file("./download.zip")),
  },
});
```

--------------------------------

### Start development server with bunx --bun vite

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/vite.mdx

Starts the Vite development server directly. The `--bun` flag forces Vite's CLI to run with Bun instead of Node.

```bash
bunx --bun vite
```

### Configure install.peer dependencies setting

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/bunfig.mdx

Controls whether bun install installs peer dependencies.

```toml
[install]
peer = true
```

Installs Bun using the Homebrew package manager on macOS or Linux.

brew install oven-sh/bun/bun
